BR-RC-1.name: BelRed Residential/Commercial Node 1
BR-RC-1.source_basis: Chart 20.25D.080.A as reproduced in Colliers offering memorandum for 1829-1831 130th Ave NE (Apr 2021), saved in phase5/work/sources; FAR 1.0 base and 4.0 max corroborated by City of Bellevue 130th TOD Feasibility Analysis (Dec 7 2018); incentive tiers per LUC 20.25D.090 code text read at bellevue.municipal.codes
BR-RC-1.notes: Node core district. Tier 1 amenity bonus 2.5 FAR plus Tier 2 0.5 FAR per LUC 20.25D.090. Ground floor retail inside the nodes is fully exempt from FAR per LUC 20.25D.080.B.3.

verification.chart_grid_basis: Chart 20.25D.080.A as reproduced in the 2021 Colliers offering memorandum, corroborated district by district against official City of Bellevue documents where one exists

far_exemptions: Floor area for affordable housing, public restrooms, and child care or nonprofit uses is not counted toward FAR (LUC 20.25D.080.B.3).

Ground floor retail meeting the LUC 20.25D.130.A criteria is not counted: inside the nodes, not counted at all; outside the nodes, tenant space is eligible up to 60 ft of depth, only in a multi-story multi-use building.
Enclosed plazas are not counted, up to 4,000 sq ft per project, with public access conditions (LUC 20.25D.080.B.3).

Land dedicated to the city for right of way, the light rail alignment, parks, or open space still counts toward the lot area used to compute maximum FAR, and the resulting floor area is transferable under LUC 20.25D.080.D to receiving sites, capped at an effective site FAR 0.5 above the receiving district maximum.
Underground buildings are not structures for floor area purposes.
Receiving district for transferred floor area under LUC 20.25D.080.D.

BR-MO.name: BelRed Medical Office
BR-MO.source_basis: Chart 20.25D.080.A reproduction (Colliers OM, Apr 2021); base FAR 1.0 corroborated by City of Bellevue staff report 16-126684-AD (Apr 7 2016); BR-MO is not listed in the incentive tiers in LUC 20.25D.090 code text (the node district BR-MO-1 is), so maximum equals base for the plain BR-MO district in the study area
BR-MO.notes: Standard residential is not permitted in BR-MO; residential uses are limited to senior housing, nursing homes, assisted living, supportive housing, hotels and motels, and ADUs (City LUCA staff analysis, Jul 8 2026). Up to 1.0 FAR of affordable housing in care projects and up to 1.0 FAR of the care use itself are exempt from FAR per LUC 20.25D.080.B.3. The separate BR-MO-1 node district (base FAR 1.0, max FAR 4.0, heights 45 and 150 ft) is not in the study area; its former polygons were rezoned MU-H by Ordinance 6847 in 2025 per the city zoning service.

open_item.title: BR-MO vs BR-MO-1 swing
open_item.detail: A City LUCA staff analysis (2026-07-08) describes the 116th Ave medical corridor, labeled BR-MO, at base FAR 1.0, max FAR 4.0, heights 45/150 ft, which are the chart values for the separate BR-MO-1 node district. The city zoning service codes the study polygons BR-MO and distinguishes BR-MO-1 where it applies, and no BR-MO-1 polygons remain (former node polygons rezoned MU-H by Ordinance 6847 in 2025). This build applies plain BR-MO (FAR 1.0 flat, 70 ft). If node standards ultimately apply, BR-MO capacity rises from 4,870 jobs to about 19,482 jobs at the maximum bound.
